---
title: Code Path Analysis Details
---

ESLint's rules can use code paths.
The code path is execution routes of programs.
It forks/joins at such as `if` statements.

```js
if (a && b) {
	foo();
}
bar();
```

:::img-container
![Code Path Example](../assets/images/code-path-analysis/helo.svg)
:::

::: tip
You can view code path diagrams for any JavaScript code using [Code Explorer](https://explorer.eslint.org).
:::

### Accessing Variable Scopes

The `SourceCode#getScope(node)` method returns the scope of the given node. It is a useful method for finding information about the variables in a given scope and how they are used in other scopes.

::: tip
You can view scope information for any JavaScript code using [Code Explorer](https://explorer.eslint.org).
:::

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
